instruments.title: Add CRR, Regulation (EU) No 575/2013
instruments.sourceLabel: EUR-Lex, Regulation (EU) No 575/2013 as published in the Official Journal

titles.en: Regulation (EU) No 575/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 26 June 2013 on prudential requirements for credit institutions and investment firms and amending Regulation (EU) No 648/2012

obligations.title: Add the duty: Maintain the minimum own funds ratios at all times
obligations.sourceLabel: EUR-Lex, Regulation (EU) No 575/2013, consolidated text of 26 June 2026, Article 92

titles.en: Maintain the minimum own funds ratios at all times

summaries.en: Institutions must at all times hold Common Equity Tier 1 capital of at least 4.5 %, Tier 1 capital of at least 6 % and total own funds of at least 8 %, each expressed as a percentage of the total risk exposure amount.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Apply the output floor when calculating the total risk exposure amount
obligations.sourceLabel: EUR-Lex, Regulation (EU) No 575/2013, consolidated text of 26 June 2026, Articles 92 and 465

titles.en: Apply the output floor when calculating the total risk exposure amount

summaries.en: Institutions must set their total risk exposure amount at no less than 72.5 % of the amount the standardised approaches would give (the output floor). During the phase-in they may use a lower factor: 50 % in 2025, 55 % in 2026, 60 % in 2027, 65 % in 2028 and 70 % in 2029.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Maintain a leverage ratio of at least 3 %
obligations.sourceLabel: EUR-Lex, Regulation (EU) No 575/2013, consolidated text of 26 June 2026, Articles 92 and 429

titles.en: Maintain a leverage ratio of at least 3 %

summaries.en: Institutions must keep their Tier 1 capital at no less than 3 % of their total exposure measure, calculated at each reporting reference date. A global systemically important institution must also hold a leverage ratio buffer in Tier 1 capital on top of that.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Calculate own funds requirements for market risk under the revised approaches
obligations.sourceLabel: EUR-Lex, Regulation (EU) No 575/2013, consolidated text of 26 June 2026, Articles 325 and 520a

titles.en: Calculate own funds requirements for market risk under the revised approaches

summaries.en: From 1 January 2027 institutions must calculate own funds requirements for market risk on all trading book positions, and on non-trading book positions carrying foreign exchange or commodity risk, using the alternative standardised approach, a permitted alternative internal model or, where eligible, the simplified standardised approach. Until then they keep applying the market risk rules as they stood on 8 July 2024.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep every exposure to a client or group of connected clients within 25 % of Tier 1 capital
obligations.sourceLabel: EUR-Lex, Regulation (EU) No 575/2013, consolidated text of 26 June 2026, Article 395

titles.en: Keep every exposure to a client or group of connected clients within 25 % of Tier 1 capital

summaries.en: An institution must not take on an exposure to a client or a group of connected clients that exceeds 25 % of its Tier 1 capital after credit risk mitigation. Where the client is an institution or investment firm the limit is 25 % of Tier 1 capital or EUR 150 million, whichever is higher, subject to an internal limit of at most 100 % of Tier 1 capital.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Report every large exposure to the competent authority
obligations.sourceLabel: EUR-Lex, Regulation (EU) No 575/2013, consolidated text of 26 June 2026, Article 394

titles.en: Report every large exposure to the competent authority

summaries.en: Institutions must report to their competent authority, for each large exposure including exempted ones, who the client or group of connected clients is and the exposure value before and after credit risk mitigation. Institutions using the internal ratings based approach also report their 20 largest exposures on a consolidated basis, and all institutions report consolidated exposures of EUR 300 million or more that are below 10 % of Tier 1 capital.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Maintain a net stable funding ratio of at least 100 %
obligations.sourceLabel: EUR-Lex, Regulation (EU) No 575/2013, consolidated text of 26 June 2026, Articles 413 and 428b

titles.en: Maintain a net stable funding ratio of at least 100 %

summaries.en: Institutions must fund their long-term assets and off-balance-sheet items with a diverse set of stable funding, keeping available stable funding at no less than 100 % of required stable funding, calculated in the reporting currency for all transactions.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Notify the competent authority and submit a restoration plan when a liquidity requirement is not met
obligations.sourceLabel: EUR-Lex, Regulation (EU) No 575/2013, consolidated text of 26 June 2026, Article 414

titles.en: Notify the competent authority and submit a restoration plan when a liquidity requirement is not met

summaries.en: An institution that does not meet, or expects not to meet, the liquidity coverage or stable funding requirement, including in times of stress, must notify its competent authority at once and submit a plan to restore compliance without undue delay. Until compliance is restored it reports the liquidity items daily, unless the authority allows a lower frequency.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Report liquidity coverage and stable funding items to the competent authority
obligations.sourceLabel: EUR-Lex, Regulation (EU) No 575/2013, consolidated text of 26 June 2026, Article 415

titles.en: Report liquidity coverage and stable funding items to the competent authority

summaries.en: Institutions must report the items of the liquidity coverage requirement at least monthly and the items of the stable funding requirement at least quarterly, in the reporting currency whatever the currency the items are denominated in.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Report own funds, leverage, large exposures, liquidity and other prudential data to the competent authority
obligations.sourceLabel: EUR-Lex, Regulation (EU) No 575/2013, consolidated text of 26 June 2026, Article 430

titles.en: Report own funds, leverage, large exposures, liquidity and other prudential data to the competent authority

summaries.en: Institutions must report to their competent authority on their own funds requirements including the leverage ratio, large exposures, liquidity requirements, aggregate data on national immovable property markets and asset encumbrance. Since 9 July 2024 the reports also cover exposures to ESG risks and crypto-asset exposures.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Publicly disclose Pillar 3 prudential information under a board-approved disclosure policy
obligations.sourceLabel: EUR-Lex, Regulation (EU) No 575/2013, consolidated text of 26 June 2026, Articles 431 to 433c

titles.en: Publicly disclose Pillar 3 prudential information under a board-approved disclosure policy

summaries.en: Institutions must publicly disclose the prudential information in Part Eight, at the frequency that fits their size and listing status (annual, semi-annual or quarterly). The management body or senior management adopts a formal disclosure policy with internal verification, and a member attests in writing that the disclosures follow it.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Submit Pillar 3 disclosures to the EBA in electronic format
obligations.sourceLabel: EUR-Lex, Regulation (EU) No 575/2013, consolidated text of 26 June 2026, Article 434

titles.en: Submit Pillar 3 disclosures to the EBA in electronic format

summaries.en: Institutions other than small and non-complex institutions must submit all their Pillar 3 disclosures electronically to the EBA no later than the date they publish their financial statements or reports for the period, or as soon as possible after. The EBA publishes them centrally.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Disclose information on environmental, social and governance risks
obligations.sourceLabel: EUR-Lex, Regulation (EU) No 575/2013, consolidated text of 26 June 2026, Article 449a

titles.en: Disclose information on environmental, social and governance risks

summaries.en: Institutions must disclose their ESG risks, separating environmental, social and governance risks and, for environmental risks, physical and transition risks. The disclosure includes total exposures to fossil fuel sector entities and how ESG risks are built into strategy, processes, governance and risk management.

instruments.title: Add CRR3, Regulation (EU) 2024/1623
instruments.sourceLabel: EUR-Lex, Regulation (EU) 2024/1623 as published in the Official Journal

titles.en: Regulation (EU) 2024/1623 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 31 May 2024 amending Regulation (EU) No 575/2013 as regards requirements for credit risk, credit valuation adjustment risk, operational risk, market risk and the output floor

instruments.title: Add LCR Delegated Regulation, Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/61
instruments.sourceLabel: EUR-Lex, Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/61 as published in the Official Journal

titles.en: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/61 of 10 October 2014 to supplement Regulation (EU) No 575/2013 of the European Parliament and the Council with regard to liquidity coverage requirement for Credit Institutions

obligations.title: Add the duty: Maintain a liquidity coverage ratio of at least 100 %
obligations.sourceLabel: EUR-Lex, Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/61, Articles 4 and 38

titles.en: Maintain a liquidity coverage ratio of at least 100 %

summaries.en: Credit institutions must keep a liquidity buffer at least equal to their net liquidity outflows over a 30-day stress period, a liquidity coverage ratio of at least 100 %. They may use the buffer in times of stress and must then follow the notification and restoration rules of Article 414 of Regulation (EU) No 575/2013. The ratio was phased in from 60 % in October 2015 to 100 % from 1 January 2018.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep the liquidity buffer diversified and ready to be monetised
obligations.sourceLabel: EUR-Lex, Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/61, Article 8

titles.en: Keep the liquidity buffer diversified and ready to be monetised

summaries.en: Credit institutions must have policies and limits that keep the liquid assets in their buffer appropriately diversified at all times, and must have ready access to those assets so they can monetise them at any time in the 30-day stress period by outright sale or repurchase agreement.

instruments.sourceLabel: EUR-Lex, Council Regulation (EU) No 1024/2013 as published in the Official Journal

titles.en: Council Regulation (EU) No 1024/2013 of 15 October 2013 conferring specific tasks on the European Central Bank concerning policies relating to the prudential supervision of credit institutions

obligations.title: Add the duty: Supply the information the ECB requests for its supervisory tasks
obligations.sourceLabel: EUR-Lex, Council Regulation (EU) No 1024/2013, Article 10

titles.en: Supply the information the ECB requests for its supervisory tasks

summaries.en: Credit institutions and their holding companies established in a participating Member State (in the Nordics, Finland) must supply the information the ECB requires for its supervisory tasks, including recurring reports in set formats. Professional secrecy does not excuse them from supplying it.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Submit to ECB on-site inspections
obligations.sourceLabel: EUR-Lex, Council Regulation (EU) No 1024/2013, Article 12

titles.en: Submit to ECB on-site inspections

summaries.en: Credit institutions and their holding companies established in a participating Member State (in the Nordics, Finland) are subject to on-site inspections at their business premises on the basis of an ECB decision, which may come without prior announcement.

instruments.title: Add SRMR, Regulation (EU) No 806/2014
instruments.sourceLabel: EUR-Lex, Regulation (EU) No 806/2014 as published in the Official Journal

titles.en: Regulation (EU) No 806/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 15 July 2014 establishing uniform rules and a uniform procedure for the resolution of credit institutions and certain investment firms in the framework of a Single Resolution Mechanism and a Single Resolution Fund and amending Regulation (EU) No 1093/2010

obligations.title: Add the duty: Meet the minimum requirement for own funds and eligible liabilities at all times
obligations.sourceLabel: EUR-Lex, Regulation (EU) No 806/2014, consolidated text of 11 June 2026, Articles 12, 12f and 12g

titles.en: Meet the minimum requirement for own funds and eligible liabilities at all times

summaries.en: Banks and groups in the banking union (in the Nordics, Finland) must meet at all times the minimum requirement for own funds and eligible liabilities (MREL) that the Single Resolution Board sets. Resolution entities meet it on a consolidated basis at resolution group level; subsidiaries that are not resolution entities meet it individually.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Report MREL information to the national resolution authority
obligations.sourceLabel: EUR-Lex, Regulation (EU) No 806/2014, consolidated text of 11 June 2026, Article 12

titles.en: Report MREL information to the national resolution authority

summaries.en: Banks and groups subject to MREL in the banking union (in the Nordics, Finland) must report their own funds and eligible liabilities information, as Article 45i of Directive 2014/59/EU describes it, to the national resolution authority of the Member State where they are established, which passes it to the Single Resolution Board.

obligations.sourceLabel: EUR-Lex, Regulation (EU) No 1093/2010, Article 16

titles.en: Make every effort to comply with EBA guidelines and recommendations

summaries.en: Financial institutions must make every effort to comply with the guidelines and recommendations the EBA issues. Where a guideline or recommendation requires it, they report clearly and in detail whether they comply.

instruments.title: Add EBA Guidelines on internal governance, EBA/GL/2021/05
instruments.sourceLabel: EBA, Guidelines on internal governance under CRD (EBA/GL/2021/05), guideline page and final report

titles.en: Guidelines on internal governance under Directive 2013/36/EU

obligations.title: Add the duty: Have the management body set, approve and oversee strategy, risk strategy and governance
obligations.sourceLabel: EBA, Final report on Guidelines on internal governance under Directive 2013/36/EU (EBA/GL/2021/05), Section 1

titles.en: Have the management body set, approve and oversee strategy, risk strategy and governance

summaries.en: The management body carries ultimate responsibility for the institution. Its duties, split between the management and supervisory functions, are set out in a written document, and it sets, approves and oversees the business strategy, the risk strategy and the internal governance framework.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Maintain an internal control framework with independent control functions
obligations.sourceLabel: EBA, Final report on Guidelines on internal governance under Directive 2013/36/EU (EBA/GL/2021/05), Sections 15 to 22

titles.en: Maintain an internal control framework with independent control functions

summaries.en: Institutions should keep a robust internal control framework in which business lines own and control their risks, supported by a risk management framework and by internal control functions (risk management, compliance and internal audit) with enough authority, stature and access to the management body.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Identify, manage and prevent conflicts of interest at institution and staff level
obligations.sourceLabel: EBA, Final report on Guidelines on internal governance under Directive 2013/36/EU (EBA/GL/2021/05), Sections 11 and 12

titles.en: Identify, manage and prevent conflicts of interest at institution and staff level

summaries.en: The management body should establish and oversee policies to identify, assess, manage and mitigate or prevent actual and potential conflicts of interest, both at institutional level and for staff, including loans and other transactions with members of the management body and their related parties.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Provide an independent internal channel for staff to report breaches
obligations.sourceLabel: EBA, Final report on Guidelines on internal governance under Directive 2013/36/EU (EBA/GL/2021/05), Section 13

titles.en: Provide an independent internal channel for staff to report breaches

summaries.en: Institutions should have internal alert policies and procedures through which staff can report potential or actual breaches of regulatory or internal requirements through a specific, independent and autonomous channel.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep a documented new product approval policy approved by the management body
obligations.sourceLabel: EBA, Final report on Guidelines on internal governance under Directive 2013/36/EU (EBA/GL/2021/05), Section 18

titles.en: Keep a documented new product approval policy approved by the management body

summaries.en: Institutions should have a well-documented new product approval policy, approved by the management body, covering new markets, products and services, significant changes to existing ones, exceptional transactions and material changes to processes and systems, so that they stay within the risk strategy and risk appetite.

instruments.title: Add EBA Guidelines on outsourcing arrangements, EBA/GL/2019/02
instruments.sourceLabel: EBA, Guidelines on outsourcing arrangements (EBA/GL/2019/02), guideline page (2019 version) and final report

titles.en: Guidelines on outsourcing arrangements

obligations.title: Add the duty: Adopt and keep up to date a written outsourcing policy
obligations.sourceLabel: EBA, Final report on EBA Guidelines on outsourcing arrangements (EBA/GL/2019/02), Section 7

titles.en: Adopt and keep up to date a written outsourcing policy

summaries.en: The management body of an institution that outsources or plans to should approve, regularly review and update a written outsourcing policy and ensure it is implemented. The policy covers the whole life cycle of outsourcing, including responsibilities, planning, monitoring, documentation and exit plans for critical or important functions.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Assess risks and carry out due diligence before entering an outsourcing arrangement
obligations.sourceLabel: EBA, Final report on EBA Guidelines on outsourcing arrangements (EBA/GL/2019/02), Section 12

titles.en: Assess risks and carry out due diligence before entering an outsourcing arrangement

summaries.en: Before entering any outsourcing arrangement, institutions should assess whether it concerns a critical or important function and whether the supervisory conditions are met, identify and assess its risks, carry out due diligence on the prospective service provider and assess any conflicts of interest.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep an up-to-date register of all outsourcing arrangements
obligations.sourceLabel: EBA, Final report on EBA Guidelines on outsourcing arrangements (EBA/GL/2019/02), Section 11

titles.en: Keep an up-to-date register of all outsourcing arrangements

summaries.en: Institutions should maintain an updated register of information on all outsourcing arrangements at individual and, where applicable, consolidated level, distinguishing critical or important functions, with at least the data points the guidelines list, and keep records of ended arrangements for an appropriate period.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Inform the competent authority of planned outsourcing of critical or important functions
obligations.sourceLabel: EBA, Final report on EBA Guidelines on outsourcing arrangements (EBA/GL/2019/02), Section 11

titles.en: Inform the competent authority of planned outsourcing of critical or important functions

summaries.en: Institutions should inform their competent authority in good time, or start a supervisory dialogue, about planned outsourcing of critical or important functions or a function that has become critical or important, and should also report material changes and severe events in their outsourcing arrangements.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep a documented exit strategy for outsourced critical or important functions
obligations.sourceLabel: EBA, Final report on EBA Guidelines on outsourcing arrangements (EBA/GL/2019/02), Section 15

titles.en: Keep a documented exit strategy for outsourced critical or important functions

summaries.en: When outsourcing critical or important functions, institutions should have a documented exit strategy in line with their outsourcing policy and business continuity plans, covering termination, failure of the provider and deteriorating service, so that they can exit without undue disruption.

instruments.title: Add EBA Guidelines on loan origination and monitoring, EBA/GL/2020/06
instruments.sourceLabel: EBA, Guidelines on loan origination and monitoring (EBA/GL/2020/06), guideline page and final report

titles.en: Guidelines on loan origination and monitoring

payload.shortName: EBA Guidelines on loan origination and monitoring

obligations.title: Add the duty: Set out and keep current credit risk policies and procedures covering all lending
obligations.sourceLabel: EBA, Final Report on Guidelines on loan origination and monitoring (EBA/GL/2020/06), Section 4.3

titles.en: Set out and keep current credit risk policies and procedures covering all lending

summaries.en: Institutions should document in their credit risk policies and procedures how they identify, assess, approve, monitor, report and mitigate credit risk, covering all lending activities, asset classes, client segments and products, and update the framework regularly.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Assess the borrower's creditworthiness before granting credit
obligations.sourceLabel: EBA, Final Report on Guidelines on loan origination and monitoring (EBA/GL/2020/06), Section 5.2

titles.en: Assess the borrower's creditworthiness before granting credit

summaries.en: Before granting a loan, institutions should analyse the application against their credit risk appetite, policies and criteria and assess the borrower's ability and prospect to meet the obligations under the agreement, based on repayment capacity rather than on collateral alone.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Price loans under a documented, risk-based pricing framework
obligations.sourceLabel: EBA, Final Report on Guidelines on loan origination and monitoring (EBA/GL/2020/06), Section 6

titles.en: Price loans under a documented, risk-based pricing framework

summaries.en: Institutions should have a documented pricing framework, supported by appropriate governance such as a pricing committee, that reflects their credit risk appetite, business strategy and the riskiness of the borrower and the loan.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Have immovable property collateral valued by a valuer at origination
obligations.sourceLabel: EBA, Final Report on Guidelines on loan origination and monitoring (EBA/GL/2020/06), Section 7

titles.en: Have immovable property collateral valued by a valuer at origination

summaries.en: At origination, institutions should have the value of all immovable property collateral assessed by an internal or external valuer with a full visit, with a desktop valuation supported by advanced statistical models allowed for residential property in well-developed markets; they then monitor and revalue the collateral.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Monitor credit exposures, borrowers and collateral through a documented framework
obligations.sourceLabel: EBA, Final Report on Guidelines on loan origination and monitoring (EBA/GL/2020/06), Section 8

titles.en: Monitor credit exposures, borrowers and collateral through a documented framework

summaries.en: Institutions should run a robust, documented credit risk monitoring framework, backed by adequate data, that keeps information on exposures, borrowers and collateral relevant and up to date and lets them manage exposures in line with their credit risk appetite.

instruments.title: Add EBA Guidelines on sound remuneration policies, EBA/GL/2021/04
instruments.sourceLabel: EBA, Guidelines on sound remuneration policies under CRD (EBA/GL/2021/04), guideline page and final report

titles.en: Guidelines on sound remuneration policies under Directive 2013/36/EU

payload.shortName: EBA Guidelines on sound remuneration policies

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep a remuneration policy for all staff adopted and overseen by the supervisory function
obligations.sourceLabel: EBA, Final report on Guidelines on sound remuneration policies under Directive 2013/36/EU (EBA/GL/2021/04), Sections 1 and 2.1

titles.en: Keep a remuneration policy for all staff adopted and overseen by the supervisory function

summaries.en: Institutions should have a remuneration policy for all staff that follows the principles of Articles 92 and 94 of Directive 2013/36/EU. The management body in its supervisory function adopts and maintains it, oversees its implementation and approves material exemptions and changes.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Identify annually the staff whose work materially affects the risk profile
obligations.sourceLabel: EBA, Final report on Guidelines on sound remuneration policies under Directive 2013/36/EU (EBA/GL/2021/04), Section 5

titles.en: Identify annually the staff whose work materially affects the risk profile

summaries.en: Institutions should carry out a self-assessment every year to identify all staff whose professional activities have or may have a material impact on the institution's risk profile, using the criteria in Article 92(3) of Directive 2013/36/EU and the regulatory technical standards on identified staff.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Set in advance the maximum ratio of variable to fixed remuneration for identified staff
obligations.sourceLabel: EBA, Final report on Guidelines on sound remuneration policies under Directive 2013/36/EU (EBA/GL/2021/04), Section 13.2

titles.en: Set in advance the maximum ratio of variable to fixed remuneration for identified staff

summaries.en: Institutions should fix in their remuneration policy, in advance, the maximum ratio between the variable and fixed components of total remuneration for identified staff, within the limits of Article 94(1)(g) of Directive 2013/36/EU and national law.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Defer part of the variable remuneration of identified staff
obligations.sourceLabel: EBA, Final report on Guidelines on sound remuneration policies under Directive 2013/36/EU (EBA/GL/2021/04), Section 15.2

titles.en: Defer part of the variable remuneration of identified staff

summaries.en: Institutions should defer part of the variable remuneration of identified staff, setting the deferral period and deferred share at or above the minimums of Article 94(1)(m) of Directive 2013/36/EU in the light of the staff member's responsibilities, the business cycle and the risks.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Be able to apply malus and clawback to all variable remuneration
obligations.sourceLabel: EBA, Final report on Guidelines on sound remuneration policies under Directive 2013/36/EU (EBA/GL/2021/04), Section 15.7.1

titles.en: Be able to apply malus and clawback to all variable remuneration

summaries.en: Institutions must be able to apply malus or clawback to up to 100 % of the total variable remuneration of identified staff, whatever the method of payment, including deferred and retained amounts.

instruments.title: Add EBA POG Guidelines, EBA/GL/2015/18
instruments.sourceLabel: EBA, Guidelines on product oversight and governance arrangements for retail banking products (EBA/GL/2015/18), guideline page (2015 version) and consolidated version of 30 June 2026

titles.en: Guidelines on product oversight and governance arrangements for retail banking products

obligations.title: Add the duty: Establish, document and regularly review product oversight and governance arrangements as a manufacturer
obligations.sourceLabel: EBA, Guidelines on product oversight and governance arrangements for retail banking products (EBA/GL/2015/18), consolidated version of 30 June 2026, Guideline 1

titles.en: Establish, document and regularly review product oversight and governance arrangements as a manufacturer

summaries.en: A firm that designs retail banking products should establish, implement and regularly review product oversight and governance arrangements so that consumers' interests, objectives and characteristics are taken into account, consumer detriment is avoided and conflicts of interest are minimised, and should document every action it takes under them.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Identify the target market and design products that meet its needs
obligations.sourceLabel: EBA, Guidelines on product oversight and governance arrangements for retail banking products (EBA/GL/2015/18), consolidated version of 30 June 2026, Guideline 3

titles.en: Identify the target market and design products that meet its needs

summaries.en: Manufacturers should identify the target market of each retail banking product, and the segments it does not suit, and only design and bring to market products whose features, charges and risks meet the interests, objectives and characteristics of, and benefit, that target market.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Test products before launch, monitor them in the market and remedy problems
obligations.sourceLabel: EBA, Guidelines on product oversight and governance arrangements for retail banking products (EBA/GL/2015/18), consolidated version of 30 June 2026, Guidelines 4 to 6

titles.en: Test products before launch, monitor them in the market and remedy problems

summaries.en: Before launching a product, selling it to a new target market or changing it significantly, manufacturers should test how it would affect consumers under a range of scenarios including stress. Once it is on the market they should monitor it continuously and act to mitigate any problem and prevent it from recurring, notifying distributors promptly.

obligations.title: Add the duty: As a distributor, build product governance into systems and controls and know the target market
obligations.sourceLabel: EBA, Guidelines on product oversight and governance arrangements for retail banking products (EBA/GL/2015/18), consolidated version of 30 June 2026, Guidelines 10 and 11

titles.en: As a distributor, build product governance into systems and controls and know the target market

summaries.en: A firm that distributes retail banking products should make product oversight and governance arrangements part of its general systems and controls, endorsed by the management body, and use the manufacturer's information to determine whether a consumer belongs to the product's target market.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep sustainability claims about retail banking products fair, clear and substantiated
obligations.sourceLabel: EBA, Guidelines on product oversight and governance arrangements for retail banking products (EBA/GL/2015/18), consolidated version of 30 June 2026, Guideline 12

titles.en: Keep sustainability claims about retail banking products fair, clear and substantiated

summaries.en: From 11 January 2027, a distributor offering products with ESG features should ensure that its sustainability-related communication is fair, clear and not misleading and that its sustainability claims are accurate, substantiated and up to date.
